title: Emissions below the operator-elicited minimum level are dropped before serialisation
asA: operator sizing log volume for a production environment
iWant: emissions below the minimum level to be dropped without serialising them
soThat: log volume matches the operator's chosen signal budget and the level filter is honoured line-by-line

acceptanceCriteria.description: With the elicited minimum level set to info, an emission at trace or debug produces no stdout line; an emission at info, warn, error or fatal produces one stdout line each. Template values the applying agent sets: The applying agent sets the elicited minimum-log-level per environment; the AC substitutes the elicited threshold for the illustrative info.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running application with minimum level set to info
acceptanceCriteria.when: one emission is issued at each of the six levels
acceptanceCriteria.then: the stdout line count equals 4 (info, warn, error, fatal), and no line at trace or debug appears

acceptanceCriteria.description: A minimum level of `fatal` drops every emission strictly below fatal, so only fatal emissions land on stdout; emissions at trace, debug, info, warn and error all produce zero lines.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running application with minimum-log-level fatal
acceptanceCriteria.when: one emission is issued at each of the six levels
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout carries exactly one line (fatal); no line for any of trace, debug, info, warn or error

acceptanceCriteria.description: Toggling the minimum level between two constructions of the factory produces the corresponding filter change; the level is fixed for the process lifetime per REQ-004 and re-reading the elicit at boot is a new factory construction, never a mid-run hook.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a factory constructed with minimum-log-level info; a second factory constructed in a subsequent process with minimum-log-level warn
acceptanceCriteria.when: one emission is issued at info under each factory
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first factory's emission lands on stdout; the second factory's emission does not; no mid-run flag flips the level in either process
